hitl_conditions: Depends on the twin's design: in decision-support mode the human keeps final decisions (digital companion); the framework also admits decision-making by AI (e.g. order placement) and control signals back to the real system; roles change through bidirectional human–twin learning.
key_finding: Proposes a 7-element SCOM digital twin framework (technology, people, management, organisation, scope, task, modelling) and five twin types; concludes twins are socio-technical systems with continuous human–AI interaction, where analytics (simulation, optimisation, neural networks, ML/RL) is the modelling backbone and decisions stay with humans or pass to AI by design.

quotes.text: the digital twin always behaves synchronously with its real counterpart, and they influence each other. It mirrors both the state and the performance of the real system and can also send control signals back to the real system.

We define the seven major elements of a digital twin in SCOM: technology, people, management, organisation, scope, task, and modelling. We also distinguish five major types of digital twins in SCOM: product, process, organisation, supply chain and network-of-networks.

Optimisation, discrete-event simulation, neural networks, machine and reinforcement learning, agent-based modelling and system dynamics allow for the implementation of the full variety of descriptive, predictive and prescriptive algorithms in SCOM.
Analytics capabilities are the backbone of digital twins. Modelling can presume decision-making support (final decisions with humans) or decision-making by AI.

Digital twins can also consider the competence of making decisions (e.g. placing orders in an inventory control system). Most centrally, digital twins offer real-time, data-driven decision-making support.

The seven elements show that digital twins in SCOM are not merely a simulation-based replica of a real object but a complex sociotechnical phenomenon involving continuous human–artificial intelligence interactions.
